Three traps on the CD IELTS Listening screen 🎧

1. The audio plays once. There is no pause and no replay, so your focus has to stay on the recording.
2. You type your answers while you listen. A spelling mistake makes the answer wrong, so practise typing words correctly under pressure.
3. The timer keeps running, even between parts. Use every pause to read the next questions.

The real exam costs about 3 million soums. Don't see this screen for the first time on exam day.

On paper, IELTS Listening gives you 10 extra minutes at the end to copy your answers onto the answer sheet.

On the computer, it doesn't. You type each answer into the box while you listen, and at the end you get only 2 minutes to check.

The timer keeps running the whole time, even between parts. So don't plan to "fix it later". Answer as you go, and use the pauses between parts to read the next questions.

Save this post for your next practice test.

Three 7s and one 5. What is your overall band? Your overall band is the average of your four sections, rounded to the nearest half band. Listening 7.0 Reading 7.0 Speaking 7.0 Writing 5.0 (7 + 7 + 7 + 5) ÷ 4 = 6.5 With Writing at 7.0, you would get 7.0. One weak section cost you half a band. Raise Writing to 6.0, and the average is 6.75, which rounds up to 7.0. Find your weakest section and fix it first. Which section would you raise first? posts.hook: Half an answer, half a band.
posts.script:
Half an answer, half a band.
Look at this Task 2 question: "Discuss both views and give your own opinion."
That is three jobs, not one.
View one. View two. Your opinion.
Many students write a great essay about one view and forget the rest.
If you skip one part, you can't get a 6 for Task Response.
Even with perfect grammar.
So before you write, underline every instruction in the question.
After each paragraph, ask yourself: which part does this answer?
Save this and check your next essay.
